title: Getting wool ready for Digital Product Passports
subtitle: What the European Digital Product Passport asks of a wool products manufacturer, how well prepared it is, and what has to happen at European level for wool to be compliant and fairly represented.
featuredImageAlt: A flock of faceted, low-poly sheep in yellow, cream and dark brown, illustrating a product passport for European wool
excerpt: Hollands Wol Collectief, a Rotterdam supplier of scoured Dutch wool and felt, explored with Regen Studio and CircularTech Forum what the Digital Product Passport means for wool. The project scored 76 data points and found that Europe's reference database holds one wool dataset, mostly Australian and New Zealand, in which one method choice can double the result. It proposes a European approach.
